summary:
S. 4745, introduced June 10, 2026, by Senator Husted (with Senator Moreno) and referred to the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, is a commemorative postal-facility naming bill.

The bill's sole operative purpose is to designate a specific United States Postal Service facility—located at 201 East Grant Avenue in Georgetown, Ohio—as the "Ulysses S. Grant Post Office Building."

Section 1(a) effects the designation. Section 1(b) provides the standard conforming reference rule: any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to that facility is deemed a reference to the "Ulysses S. Grant Post Office Building."

The bill amends no existing statute or provision of the U.S. Code, creates no new agency authority, and contains no authorization of appropriations, appropriation, sunset, or delegated rulemaking. It includes no effective-date provision, deadline, condition precedent, or material exception; by default the designation would take effect upon enactment.
